PAF Reading Program’s beautifully illustrated beginning readers contain decodable and controlled stories. The decodable text only contains sounds that have been taught, so that children can sound out words. There is a repetition of vocabulary to develop the recognition of common words, and the length of words, the complexity of sentences, and the amount of text in each chapter gradually increase. The books provide the practice needed to develop accuracy and fluency as well as reading stamina. Coherent narratives have all the basic elements of good storytelling­ —characters, setting, plot, conflict, and resolution. They support the teaching of effective comprehension strategies in engaging ways. Best of all, children love the adventures and humor!
Take a peek at some sample chapters!

Skills Books Skills Books provide activities in phonemic awareness, decoding, word recognition, spelling, handwriting, vocabulary, and comprehension. They are meant to be used under teacher supervision with discussion and immediate feedback. Teacher Editions Teacher Editions provide prompts to support children’s engagement and understanding of the stories. The resulting class discussions encourage logical reasoning, making inferences, and a range of comprehension strategics including rereading, paraphrasing, and summarizing. 42
